_source: Standard gas-phase electronic absorption assignments for four small molecules, entered by hand. Chosen so a reader can check them without a database, the same way benchmarks/ir/reference.json was built. Formaldehyde, acetone and benzene reproduce the values already recorded in docs/ROADMAP.md's TD-DFT section, so the control arm can be checked against a figure this project measured itself.
_units: Excitation energies in eV, VERTICAL. Oscillator strengths are dimensionless. Computed values from ORCA's ABSORPTION SPECTRUM VIA TRANSITION ELECTRIC DIPOLE MOMENTS block, which reports fosc(D2).

_f_kinds.measured: an experimental oscillator strength, scored against |ratio| <= 2x
_f_kinds.estimated: a literature figure that is approximate or model-dependent; scored the same way but flagged
_f_kinds.forbidden: electric-dipole forbidden by symmetry, observed only vibronically. Scored as 'the computation must also report it as ~zero' (f <= 0.01), NOT as a ratio -- 2x of zero is zero and would be unfalsifiable
_f_kinds.absent: no oscillator strength I can state from a source. Intensity scores as UNAVAILABLE for that transition rather than being manufactured
_f_kinds.unsourced: a value IS in circulation but its provenance did not survive checking, and the candidates disagree enough to change the verdict. Scores as UNAVAILABLE like 'absent', but carries the candidates and what each implies, because 'we do not know' and 'nobody has looked' are different states and collapsing them loses the fact that somebody looked

_identification.why: A transition is located by DECLARED orbital character, never by nearest energy. Matching on energy would use the answer to find the thing being scored, which is exactly the circularity that let an 8-root run report benzene's strongest band as missing while producing plausible numbers.
_identification.donor: Occupied MO indices RELATIVE TO HOMO: 0 = HOMO, -1 = HOMO-1. HOMO is read from the ORBITAL ENERGIES block as the last row with OCC 2.0000.
_identification.acceptor: Virtual MO indices RELATIVE TO LUMO: 0 = LUMO, +1 = LUMO+1.
_identification.kind_orbital: Exactly one root's dominant contribution must lie in the declared donor/acceptor sets. More than one, or none, is UNSCORABLE.
_identification.kind_orbital_rank: Several states share one orbital character and cannot be told apart by it -- benzene's B2u, B1u and E1u all come from the same four HOMO/HOMO-1 -> LUMO/LUMO+1 excitations in different linear combinations. Those are ranked by computed energy WITHIN the matching set, which is a declared rule rather than a fit to the experimental answer. A rank that does not exist is UNSCORABLE.
_identification.require_degenerate: Defaults true when degeneracy > 1, and pyridine is why it can be turned off. Benzene's 1E1u MUST be degenerate -- D6h requires it -- so a computation that splits it is saying something is wrong, and enforcing that is a real check. Pyridine's analogue MUST NOT be: the nitrogen lowers the symmetry to C2v and lifts the degeneracy, measured at 0.244 / 0.122 / 0.082 eV across three arms. It is still ONE observed band and is summed like a degenerate pair, but refusing it for not being degenerate would be refusing correct chemistry. The reported energy is INTENSITY-WEIGHTED so a split band reports where its absorption maximum is; for a truly degenerate pair that is identical to the plain mean, so benzene pays nothing for it.
_identification.degeneracy: How many roots form the band. A degenerate set must actually be degenerate in the computation (energies within DEGENERACY_TOLERANCE_EV) or the result is UNSCORABLE rather than averaged, and its oscillator strength is SUMMED across the components.
_identification.why_f_is_summed: An experimental oscillator strength is obtained by integrating ONE absorption band, and two degenerate components lie at the same energy and cannot be separated in that integral -- so the experimental figure is the band total and the computed quantity to compare with it is the sum. Getting this wrong costs exactly a factor of the degeneracy, which is precisely why it hides: ROADMAP.md compared ONE of benzene's two 1E1u components (0.9607) against the band's experimental figure and concluded the intensity was 'essentially correct', when summing gives 1.9212. NOTE the SIZE of the resulting error is not settled here and this note deliberately no longer states one -- that depends on the reference value, which is 'unsourced'. score.py prints components AND their sum so the two conventions can never be silently mixed again.

transitions.label: n->pi* (1A2)
transitions.note: 1A2 <- 1A1 is electric-dipole forbidden in C2v; the band is seen vibronically. ROADMAP records B3LYP/def2-SVP at 4.078 eV against this 4.07, and notes the computed f came back essentially zero, which is correct rather than a failure.

formaldehyde.strongest_note: Formaldehyde's strongest absorption is the pi->pi* near 8 eV, which sits among Rydberg states that def2-SVP has no diffuse functions to place. Scoring a strongest-band identity here would be measuring the basis set's Rydberg problem rather than the functional, so this molecule scores position and intensity only.

transitions.label: n->pi* (1A2)
transitions.note: Same forbidden n->pi* as formaldehyde, red-shifted by the two methyls. ROADMAP records B3LYP/def2-SVP at 4.444 eV, and that def2-SVPD moved it only to 4.45 -- so this transition is insensitive to diffuse functions and is the control for 'the change did nothing here'.

acetone.strongest_note: As formaldehyde: the strong band is out of the region def2-SVP can be trusted for.

transitions.label: 1B2u

f.measured_source: Bolovinos, Tsekeris, Philis, Pantos and Andritsopoulos, J. Mol. Spectrosc. 103 (1984) 240-256, doi:10.1016/0022-2852(84)90051-1 Table I (f^a = 0.13 x 10^-2)

transitions.note: Forbidden in D6h, observed vibronically (~253 nm). ROADMAP: def2-SVP 5.49, def2-SVPD 5.40.

transitions.label: 1B1u

f.measured_source: Bolovinos, Tsekeris, Philis, Pantos and Andritsopoulos, J. Mol. Spectrosc. 103 (1984) 240-256, doi:10.1016/0022-2852(84)90051-1 Table I (f^a = 9.0 x 10^-2)
f.why_still_forbidden: MEASURED AT 0.090, WHICH IS NOT ZERO -- and the computation is still right to return 0. 1B1u <- 1A1g is electric-dipole forbidden in D6h and borrows its intensity vibronically, which a VERTICAL calculation at a fixed geometry cannot produce by construction. Scoring the computed 0.0000 against the measured 0.090 would fail the computation for a limitation of the vertical approximation rather than for being wrong, so the criterion stays 'must come back dark' and the measurement is recorded beside it.

transitions.note: Also forbidden in D6h (~200 nm). ROADMAP: def2-SVP 6.47, def2-SVPD 6.31.

transitions.label: 1E1u

f.source: Bolovinos, Tsekeris, Philis, Pantos and Andritsopoulos, J. Mol. Spectrosc. 103 (1984) 240-256, doi:10.1016/0022-2852(84)90051-1 Table I -- an ABSOLUTE measurement, f^a = 0.90 at eps_max 6.96 eV

transitions.note: SOURCED 2026-08-12 AND THE ANSWER WAS THE ORIGINAL ONE. This carried kind:unsourced with candidates 0.9 and 1.25 because a web summary attributed 1.25 to the CASPT2 benzene study. Reading that paper, '1.25' DOES NOT APPEAR IN IT -- it says the experimental values are 'scattered in the range 0.6-1.05' with its own graphical integration giving 0.80, and that 0.80 includes the A2u Rydberg band. Bolovinos Table I then gives the direct absolute measurement, f = 0.90, which is what ROADMAP.md carried all along without a citation. Refusing to write 1.25 in on a search summary was the right call. THE BAND THIS WHOLE BENCHMARK EXISTS FOR -- the allowed, intense pi->pi* near 180 nm, doubly degenerate. ROADMAP: def2-SVP puts it at 7.918 eV with f = 0.9607 (intensity right, position 0.98 eV high); def2-SVPD at 7.430 eV with f = 0.0832 (position better, intensity an order of magnitude too weak). Degeneracy 2, so the computed f is SUMMED across the pair before comparison.

benzene.strongest_note: 1E1u is declared strongest explicitly rather than derived from 'the band at experimental lambda_max'. The two are related but not identical claims, and the whole def2-SVPD failure is a case where a code that conflated them would have scored it as passing.

pyridine._sourced: SOURCED 2026-08-12 from Bolovinos et al., J. Mol. Spectrosc. 103 (1984) 240-256, doi:10.1016/0022-2852(84)90051-1, and no longer provisional. Table I gives the pi->pi* eps_max energies and oscillator strengths; Table III gives the n->pi*. Energies below are eps_max (the band MAXIMUM) rather than the 0-0 origin, because a vertical excitation energy is what the computation reports. The paper also settles a decision this file had already taken on symmetry grounds: pyridine's E1u-derived bands 'do not show any splitting due to the lifting of the 1E1u degeneracy', i.e. experiment sees ONE band where the computation resolves two -- which is exactly why they are summed under require_degenerate:false.

transitions.label: n->pi* (1B1)

f.source: Bolovinos et al., J. Mol. Spectrosc. 103 (1984) 240-256, doi:10.1016/0022-2852(84)90051-1 Table III, f x 10^-3 = 3, at eps_max 4.59 eV (their 0-0 origin is 4.310 eV)

transitions.note: 11a1(n) -> 3b1(pi*), x-polarised and therefore ALLOWED though weak -- which is why the computation gives it a small non-zero f rather than zero. Table III lists the neighbouring 1A1 -> 1A2 as forbidden, and that is the dark second root the computation produces; the ordering assumed here is the paper's.

transitions.label: pi->pi* (1B2u-like)

f.source: Bolovinos et al., J. Mol. Spectrosc. 103 (1984) 240-256, doi:10.1016/0022-2852(84)90051-1 Table I, f^a = 2.9 x 10^-2 at eps_max 4.99 eV

transitions.note: Benzene's 1B2u with the nitrogen making it weakly allowed rather than forbidden -- f = 0.029 against benzene's 0.0013.

transitions.label: pi->pi* (1B1u-like)

f.source: Bolovinos et al., J. Mol. Spectrosc. 103 (1984) 240-256, doi:10.1016/0022-2852(84)90051-1 Table I, f^a = 8.5 x 10^-2 at eps_max 6.38 eV

transitions.note: Benzene's 1B1u analogue. Note this is the one band in the whole benchmark the computation gets too WEAK rather than too strong -- measured 0.085 against a computed 0.022-0.031.

transitions.label: pi->pi* (1E1u-like pair)

f.source: Bolovinos et al., J. Mol. Spectrosc. 103 (1984) 240-256, doi:10.1016/0022-2852(84)90051-1 Table I, f^a = 0.90 at eps_max 7.22 eV

transitions.note: The intense band, benzene's 1E1u with the degeneracy lifted by the nitrogen. THE ENERGY WAS GUESSED AT ~7.0 BEFORE IT WAS SOURCED and is 7.22, which matters: it moved pyridine's error from +1.04..+1.27 to +0.82..+1.05, i.e. onto benzene's +0.84..+1.10 rather than beside it. Summed across the two computed components because the paper reports the splitting as unresolved.
transitions._correction: THIS DECLARED rank 3 AND SCORED THE WRONG BAND. rank 3 is the B2u-like band at 4.99 eV, now scored in its own right above. The strongest-band check reported FAIL rather than scoring it quietly, which is what identifying by declared orbital character exists for. Ranks measured stable across all three arms; WHICH of ranks 5 and 6 is brighter varies by arm, so a single rank would have been fitting to one output.

pyridine.strongest_note: Declared from the measurement: Table I makes the E1u-like band the strongest by an order of magnitude (f = 0.90 against 0.085 and 0.029).
